sourceInformation.genre: Space combat simulation; tactical arcade shooter
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person cockpit, with optional third-person chase camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with native WebGL2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; bundled single HTML
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded spacecraft and planets, ink outlines, print grain, ivory and amber flight instruments
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer / AnimationClip keyframe tracks for station rings, enemy reactors, engine pulses, weapon recoil and explosions; procedural flight motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synthesizer music at 10% default music volume; synthesized effects; formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish radio voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub ghost patrol races for 1–4 pilots; standalone two-pilot WebRTC link-code race; BroadcastChannel same-browser link
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted headless testing; screenshots only for visual composition. 74/74 checks: Chromium 153 WebGPU framebuffer/readback and WebGL2, complete scripted patrol, standard gamepad stub, Pixel 7 multitouch, WebKit iPhone stand-in, offline Web Audio, real two-page WebRTC, local tab link, and three official AI Hub harness scenarios.
sourceInformation.research: none; no internet research. Downloaded only dependencies and the user-supplied AI Hub integration contract and harness

testingFeedback: 5 game issues found and fixed: toon-material setup warnings, live-tuning units, renderer recovery disposal, an unconnected radio voice trigger, and a clipped portrait title. Test-script setup corrections are excluded.
1 game-breaking issue: restarting gameplay after a lost graphics device could throw during resource disposal. Recovery now retires the old renderer’s resources before switching to WebGL2.

The fixed-step full-operation playthrough: actual Rapier cannon hits cleared all 15 enemies, broke both relays, destroyed the command ship and returned to a repaired dock. The official multiplayer harness added network lifecycle coverage.

Early WebGPU screenshots: the headless compositor could show a blank/white canvas despite submitted draws. Native offscreen framebuffer readback and state assertions are more reliable; WebGL2 screenshots were used to judge composition.
engineFeedback: Native scene graphs, toon materials and AnimationMixer support a consistent procedural art style.

Yes. MeshToonNodeMaterial does not accept flatShading as a constructor option, and renderer replacement required disposing live scene resources before retiring the old backend. Software WebGPU also needed both ANGLE and Vulkan launch flags.
The cockpit flight model, tactical campaign, combat systems, user interface and multiplayer race logic.
Managing WebGPU device loss, render-resource lifetimes and headless presentation while keeping the flight simulation independent.
Make backend replacement dispose its listeners safely, and expose a clearer first-frame/readback readiness API for headless verification.
promptFeedback: The source, controller-first constraints and complete vertical-slice requirement gave the game a clear identity.
Standalone multiplayer transport was unspecified; I chose peer-to-peer link codes and an optional local tab link.
Making tactical navigation, free flight, combat, docking and multiplayer feel coherent in one self-contained file.
Specify whether standalone multiplayer needs automatic room discovery or whether manual peer-to-peer pairing is acceptable.

aiHub.name: Star Reclaimers
aiHub.description: Defend Kestrel in an ink-stroked space patrol. Manage energy, jump six sectors, dock for repairs, and tear down the Crown command ship; compare scores with wingmates in a ghost patrol race.
aiHub.controls: Mouse aim, WASD fly, click/Space fire, Shift boost, C shield, X nova, T target, F dock, M chart, J jump, V camera, Esc pause; standard gamepad; assisted touch.
